correctness.rationale: The unit ball of H_n is the convex hull of ±(e_i−e_j)/2; thus ||R||=D/2. Every extension is a common translation of the n image columns, so its minimum norm is exactly their ℓ1 Chebyshev radius. The arithmetic mean gives r≤(n−1)D/n. For n=2k the balanced-subset incidence signs yield m=C(n,k), pairwise distance D=4C(n−2,k−1)=nm/(n−1), and each coordinate has k signs of each type. Scalar median inequality forces any center to have maximal ℓ1 radius at least m, attained at center zero. Together give exact factor 2(n−1)/n, including n=2. Exhaustive exact finite checks n=2,4,6,8,10,12 corroborate combinatorics; the proof is uniform in n.

value.rationale: POE-1 is a natural quantitative invariant governing whether inclusion-induced free Banach lattice maps are bounded below. This theorem determines the *optimal* extension loss for an entire canonical codimension-one family in all even dimensions and gives concrete finite targets realizing the obstruction; qualitative POE membership and generic projection bounds do not determine the sharp constant. The balanced-cut configurations explain the extremality geometrically and show the loss approaches two even though every source hyperplane is finite-dimensional. The computation is not an arbitrary slice: it uses the standard zero-sum hyperplane and exactly the ℓ1 targets appearing in the POE-1 definition.
